UK rule: Interest and fees on high-cost short-term credit (HCSTC, "payday") must not exceed 0.8% per day of the amount borrowed. In force since 2 Jan 2015.
citation: FCA press release 11 Nov 2014; CONC 5A (FCA Handbook)

UK rule: Default charges must not exceed £15 (fixed).
citation: FCA press release 11 Nov 2014; CONC 5A

UK rule: Borrower never repays more in interest and fees than the amount borrowed (100% of principal).
citation: FCA press release 11 Nov 2014; CONC 5A

UK rule: 2017 review kept the cap. 2026 review: stakeholders broadly backed the cap; in Sept 2026 the FCA decided not to proceed to stage 2 (data analysis) and will monitor instead. Cap unchanged.
citation: FCA HCSTC page, updated 06/10/2026

UK rule: Total credit charges capped at 100% of the product's base price; base price benchmarked to mainstream retailers; no recouping via insurance or arrears charges. In force 1 Apr 2019.
citation: FCA PS19/6; CONC 5B (verify chapter still live in 2026)

UK rule: A pawn is redeemable at any time within 6 months after it was taken (parties may agree a period equal to the credit term, or longer). After that it stays redeemable until realised (sold), unless title has passed.
citation: Consumer Credit Act 1974 s.116 (legislation.gov.uk, up to date to 12 Nov 2026)

parameter: Pawn: title passes on small loans
UK rule: If the credit is ≤ £75 (fixed-sum, or running-account limit ≤ £75) and redemption period is 6 months, unredeemed property passes to the pawnbroker. Otherwise it becomes "realisable" (must be sold under s.121).

Before selling, give the pawnor notice (min. 14 days) with asking price; after sale give written info on proceeds and expenses. Surplus goes back to the customer; shortfall stays as debt. Pawnbroker must prove reasonable care to get true market value.
citation: CCA 1974 s.121; Consumer Credit (Realisation of Pawn) Regs 1983 (SI 1983/1568)

UK rule: Original text: no pre-sale notice needed if credit ≤ £50. Secondary sources say £100. See Part D.
citation: SI 1983/1568 reg 3 (as made)

UK rule: Pawnbroking is regulated consumer credit (lending against a pledge). It needs FCA consumer credit lending permission. Pawn loans are OUTSIDE the HCSTC price cap: the HCSTC definition (APR ≥ 100%, repayable within 12 months) excludes credit secured by a mortgage, charge or pledge. So pawn has no price cap. CONC conduct rules + Consumer Duty apply.
citation: CCA 1974 Part VIII ss.114–122; FCA Glossary "high-cost short-term credit" (G3328) via FCA FOI5715 response. Pawn-specific FCA guidance not retrieved: see Part D

UK rule: Lending under a regulated consumer credit agreement is a regulated activity. A non-bank lender needs FCA Part 4A permission (consumer credit "lending" permission). Lenders are solo-regulated by the FCA (not PRA) unless they take deposits.
citation: FSMA 2000 s.19 general prohibition + Part 4A; FCA "Guide for consumer credit firms" (fca.org.uk)

UK rule: Firm must meet FCA threshold conditions on an ongoing basis, including "appropriate resources" (COND 2.4: financial and non-financial resources adequate for the business), suitability, effective supervision, business model.
citation: FSMA (Threshold Conditions) Order 2013; FCA Handbook COND 2.4; PRIN Principle 4 (adequate financial resources)

UK rule: No fixed minimum capital ratio for ordinary consumer credit lenders. Only general "appropriate resources" + Principle 4. MIPRU applies to mortgage/insurance intermediaries, not to consumer credit lenders; IFPRU no longer exists (replaced by MIFIDPRU for investment firms). FCA says its capital focus in consumer credit is debt management firms and P2P platforms.
citation: FCA Guide for consumer credit firms; CONC 10.1 (scope). MIPRU/MIFIDPRU scope not separately fetched: see Part D

UK rule: Debt management firms (and not-for-profit debt advice bodies holding ≥ £1m client money) must hold prudential resources = 0.25% of first £5m of relevant debts under management + 0.15% of next £95m + 0.05% above, minimum £5,000; recalc if debts under management rise > 15%.
citation: CONC 10.1–10.3 (FCA Handbook)

UK rule: Since 28 Jan 2021: ban on motor finance (HP and conditional sale) commission models where broker commission is linked to the interest rate AND the broker can set/adjust that rate. Rate-for-risk models still allowed; consumer hire not covered. Commission that varies by lender/product must be disclosed prominently.
citation: FCA PS20/8 (Jul 2020); CONC 4.5.6R (ban), CONC 4.5.3R (disclosure)

parameter: Supreme Court ruling (Johnson v FirstRand, Hopcraft/Wrench)
UK rule: [2025] UKSC 33, 1 Aug 2025. Dealers did NOT owe customers a fiduciary duty, so bribery claims (tort/equity) failed. But in Johnson the relationship was UNFAIR under CCA s.140A (large undisclosed commission, undisclosed tie to lender); commission repaid with interest. s.140A test is broad and fact-sensitive.
citation: UK Supreme Court judgment/press summary UKSC 2024/0157-0159

UK rule: Final rules PS26/3 published 29/30 Mar 2026, in force 31 Mar 2026. Scope: regulated motor finance agreements 6 Apr 2007 – 1 Nov 2024 where commission was paid. FCA page: est. £7.5bn redress; firms/law-firm summaries: ~12.1m agreements, avg ~£829, total ~£9.1bn incl. costs. Implementation to 30 Jun 2026 (loans from 1 Apr 2014) and 31 Aug 2026 (earlier). **Partly suspended since 2 Jul 2026** by the Upper Tribunal (challengers: Consumer Voice, VW FS, Mercedes-Benz FS, CA Auto Finance). Firms need not calculate/pay redress on the timetable until the Tribunal finishes; must still identify cases, gather data, plan for a no-scheme scenario with capital/liquidity. Hearing 14–18 Dec 2026 or 16–26 Feb 2027.
citation: FCA PS26/3 page (updated 3 Jul 2026); FCA statement "Motor finance scheme partially suspended" (2 Jul 2026)

UK rule: Before the agreement, lender must do a reasonable creditworthiness assessment of the guarantor's ability to meet the guarantee (CONC 5.2A.31R) and give the guarantor an adequate explanation of when the guarantee may be called (CONC 4.2.22R). Arrears rules (CONC 7.3) apply to guarantors too. No price cap unless the loan is HCSTC.
citation: FCA response to FSB super-complaint (05/03/2024, updated 13/01/2026), citing CONC 5.2A.31R, 4.2.22R, 7.3.2G

UK rule: Still governed by Bills of Sale Act 1878 and (1878) Amendment Act 1882 (no repeal shown on legislation.gov.uk). Bill must follow the statutory form (s.9) and be registered within 7 clear days (s.8); void if consideration < £30 (s.12); seizure only on listed grounds (s.7), with s.7A limits for regulated consumer credit. Not enforceable in Scotland. Also regulated consumer credit, so CONC + Consumer Duty apply. Goods Mortgages Bill (Law Commission) never enacted.
citation: legislation.gov.uk Vict/45-46/43; Law Commission Goods Mortgages Bill pages

UK rule: Before lending or raising a limit, lender must assess creditworthiness: both credit risk to the lender and affordability for the customer (repay without financial difficulty), proportionate to the loan. Same rule for banks and non-banks (CONC applies to all consumer credit firms). Extended to BNPL (deferred payment credit) from 15 Jul 2026, including under £50.
citation: FCA Handbook CONC 5.2A (CONC sourcebook Feb 2026); FCA PS26/1 (BNPL) via Grant Thornton summary

UK rule: Applies to all FCA-authorised firms incl. non-bank lenders: open products from 31 Jul 2023, closed books from 31 Jul 2024. Four outcomes (products/services, price & value, understanding, support).
citation: FCA PS22/9; FCA Dear CEO letter consumer finance closed products (16 May 2024); FG25/2

UK rule: Since 4 Nov 2024 (PS24/2): firms must consider appropriate support for customers in, or at risk of, payment difficulty; forbearance options incl. sustainable repayment arrangements; priority debts and essential living expenses (mortgage, rent, council tax, food, utilities) to be considered. Coronavirus guidance withdrawn. Same CONC 7 for banks (overdrafts) and non-banks.
citation: FCA PS24/2; FCA 2024/7 Tailored Support Instrument; CONC 7.3

UK rule: Accepting deposits (where deposits are lent on or fund the business) is a regulated activity (RAO art.5). Doing it needs a Part 4A permission granted by the PRA (with FCA consent); the firm becomes a dual-regulated bank. A finance house without it must fund via equity, wholesale lines, securitisation, etc.
citation: RAO 2001 (SI 2001/544) art.5 (up to date to 12 Nov 2026); FSMA s.19; Bank of England New Bank Start-Up Unit pages

UK rule: Same conduct rules (CONC 5.2A, CONC 7, Consumer Duty, CCA). Differences: (1) no deposits; (2) no PRA capital/liquidity rules (CRR/Basel) for non-banks, only COND 2.4 "appropriate resources"; (3) non-banks are FCA solo-regulated; (4) banks with deposits fall under FSCS deposit protection and ring-fencing thresholds.
citation: Derived from rows above; ring-fencing/FSCS not separately sourced in this round
